newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - New issues spark little interest.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - New issues spark little interest.

text.p: Initial public offerings met with a cool reception this week, though a couple of deals scheduled to be priced later Thursday for trading on Friday -- such as U.S. Rentals Inc and Brylane Inc -- may brighten the mood.

John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, said investors' attention was focused on blue-chip stocks, not new issues, during the shortened holiday week. "The spotlight is on another corner in the floating crap game called Wall Street," he said.

Four deals have made their debuts so far this week. Three garnered no more than a small premium over their offering prices, which had been revised downward in two cases. One deal "broke issue" or fell below its offering price.
Shares of Micro Therapeutics Inc, which were priced at $6, closed at 6-1/4 on Wednesday. The initial range on the 1.6 million share issue, lead-managed by UBS Securities, was $11 to $13 per share.
The California-based company makes minimally invasive medical devices for the diagnosis and treatment of vascular disease.

Apex PC Solutions Inc shares were priced at $9, at the lower end of their $9 to $11 range, and closed unchanged on Wednesday after reaching an intraday high of 9-5/8. The shares were at 9-1/8 in midday trading on Thursday.
Analysts had expected the 3.5 million share deal, led by Montgomery Securities, to jump around two points at its opening.
Apex supplies centralized consoles to manage personal computers that are interconnected in client/server networks.

VDI Media Inc's 2.8 million-share offering was priced at $7 per share, within the $6.50 to $7.50 revised range. The Hollywood, Calif.-based company, which duplicates and distributes broadcast videos, had started off with a range of $10 to $12.
Shares rose to 8, and then closed at 7-3/8 on Wednesday, They were up 3/8 at 7-3/4 by midday Thursday. The deal was managed by Prudential Securities.

Shares of Complete Wellness Centers Inc, a medical center developer, dipped below their offering price of $6 to close on Wednesday at $5. The deal, managed by National Securities, consisted of one million shares.
